board_formula: board = 1 + 38*(x - right_x)/(left_x - right_x); 'board' uses edges at the ball centre row y (as prescribed), 'board_contact' at the contact row y+r
method: Each path point is one source frame: the ball circle and, in that same frame, the left and right wood edges (where the olive/yellow wood meets the dark gutter channel) at the ball centre row y and at the contact row y+r, snapped to the strongest grey-level gradient within +-8-14 px of an eye prior and checked on a gridded lane strip (no quad carried between frames). Entry = median of six named reads: contact-row edge profile at pin_hit-1/0/+1, the 7-column pin ruler (7-pin..10-pin = 36 in, physical boards 36.5..3.5 under the task's board formula) at 442 and 444, and an 8.5 in = 7.8 board ball-diameter ruler from the right edge at 443.
limits: Far-end edges +-1-2 px on a ~95 px lane (+-0.4-0.8 board); the ball centre +-1 px for r~10. Centre-row vs contact-row reads differ by 0-1 board (contact row is the geometrically correct one; 'board' keeps the prescribed centre row). The pin ruler uses physical column boards 36.5/31.0/25.5/20/14.5/9.0/3.5; the task text's '7-pin on 33, 10-pin on 7' mapping would read 11.2 at f442 and is not used. Scale conflict persists: 7 pin columns span 59 px (1.64 px/in) while the wood is ~90 px (2.15 px/in) and the ball diameter ~20 px (2.35 px/in); the pin ruler still lands within 0.3 board of the edge reads because the rack sits right-of-centre between the edges (left gap ~20 px, right gap ~10 px). Ball-diameter ruler: r 10.3 +-0.5 px -> +-5 % scale. pin_row_frame 443 (+-1: at 442 the centre is 1.4 px below the lowest pin bases at y~640). Loop-1 board formula was 39*(r-x)/(r-l), about 0.5 board off this one; do not 'correct' loop-1 reads with it.
